decision_reason: A1 provides only one-coordinate distinctions for standing still versus sitting and relaxing, walking versus jogging, and knees bending (crouching) versus waist bends forward. Add ankle_posture_variability to distinguish lower-limb participation in crouching from predominantly trunk bending, with climbing stairs and cycling as transferable seen anchors. Do not manufacture an additional standing-versus-sitting distinction: the available chest and ankle placements do not directly observe seated thigh orientation, and both activities can have upright chests and similar ankle orientations. Likewise, do not infer flight phases or precise gait mechanics to separate walking from jogging. Remove motion_regularity because its A1 value is identical across all classes and therefore supplies no split-specific semantic contrast. The supplied coverage diagnostics guide these priorities but do not establish predictability or recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: ankle_posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent of change in the gravity-relative orientation of the body segment carrying the left ankle sensor within a window, excluding rotation that leaves its gravity-relative inclination unchanged.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude across the available sensors. Preserve the existing walking-versus-jogging distinction and static-versus-active transfer. Execution effort and speed can blur ordinal boundaries; no additional gait distinction is assumed.

cadence: G6 supports recurring ankle, arm or chest motion rates. Repetition rate transfers from seen cyclic activities to walking and repeated crouching independently of motion magnitude. Slow repetitions, pauses and short windows can obscure the meaningful cycle or produce harmonic ambiguity.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in acceleration, distinguishing continuously executed movements from persistently fluctuating motion. Retain this transferable temporal-quality concept, but do not treat the existing crouching-versus-waist-bending difference as guaranteed: movement technique and speed can reverse or weaken it.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes, particularly at the ankle during contacts and at the chest during transmitted impacts. This provides transfer between locomotion, jumping and comparatively non-impact bending. Footwear, landing technique and isolated nonrepresentative movements can alter peak strength.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative mean orientation, with chest acceleration providing evidence about torso attitude. Lying down supplies a seen horizontal-posture anchor for static unseen activities. Chest attitude is only a proxy for global configuration: upright sitting and standing can look alike, so the A1 distinction must not be interpreted as assured sensor-level separation.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative posture, with chest orientation changes providing evidence of global reconfiguration. Preserve bending-based transfer to crouching and separation from static postures. A relatively upright trunk during crouching can underrepresent global configuration changes, while dynamic acceleration can obscure gravity.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular motion directly at the right lower arm and left ankle. Preserve broad rotation prominence for transfer among limb exercises, cycling and crouching. Chest rotation is not directly measured by a chest gyroscope, and rotation localized to unsensed joints can be weakly represented; this attribute alone cannot reliably separate crouching from waist bending.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion proxies from the available accelerometers. Preserve the semantic distinction between locomotion and largely stationary exercises, transferring jogging and stair-climbing semantics to walking. Local limb displacement, cyclic reversals and unobservable constant velocity limit inference of sustained progression; do not interpret this as measured travel distance.

G11 could support temporal recurrence and predictability, but every supplied A1 prototype assigns motion_regularity High. It therefore adds no contrast for any activity pair in this split. Drop it for compactness rather than inventing unsupported class differences; cadence remains a distinct rate concept, not a replacement claim about predictability.

ankle_posture_variability: G12 supports gravity-relative orientation excursions, with G2 providing corroborating ankle rotation evidence. Changing inclination at the left ankle can expose lower-limb participation during crouching that is absent or smaller during predominantly waist-driven bending, adding a localized distinction beyond their shared global posture variation. Climbing stairs and cycling provide seen examples of lower-limb orientation change, while waist bends forward provides a contrasting anchor. This is segment inclination, not inferred knee angle or squat depth. Foot placement, crouching technique, ankle attachment and dynamic acceleration can weaken the contrast; use broad ordinal excursions rather than fine joint mechanics. It is not proposed as a standing-versus-sitting discriminator.

semantic_redundancy_review: The nine outputs retain distinct physical meanings. Motion intensity measures magnitude, cadence repetition rate, smoothness sustained rapid fluctuation, and impulsiveness isolated abrupt peaks. Mean global inclination differs from global posture variation. Rotational prominence does not specify gravity-relative excursion, and translational progression is not equivalent to limb rotation. The added ankle_posture_variability deliberately localizes posture change: it can vary independently of global posture variability during limb-dominant versus trunk-dominant movements. This localization adds a plausible crouching-versus-waist-bending contrast without claiming direct knee-angle measurement. Standing still versus sitting and relaxing remains a genuine observability limitation rather than being separated through an unsupported attribute. All-pair review does not justify additional fine-grained gait, flight, support-contact or displacement attributes from the supplied capabilities.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
